Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Center Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/18/2021
Comments: On 3/18/21 at 1153 hrs., I conducted an inspection of DiversifiedProduction, LLC's F Kinter 3 well (API 063-35436) in Center Twp., Indiana Co. in response to a reported release of 42.5 barrels of production fluid onto the ground from a tank located onsite. According to the operator, corroded threads on a coupling connected to the tank was the cause of the release. Photos were submitted to the Department prior to inspection of the site. The release impacted the earthen berm containment area and a portion of an agricultural field to the north of the berm. Conductivity readings were elevated both within the earthen berm and outside the berm, indicating migration through the berm and soil in the adjacent field. The operator had tentatively delineated the northern extent of the migration with yellow flags. Soil conductivity beyond the northern most flag was at background level. The operator notified the Department that remediation of the site would commence on Monday, 3/22/21. The release of production fluids from a tank onto the ground constitutes violations of SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1), and 78.57(a). The violations associated with this release will be resolved upon remediation of the site and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Please refer to Page 3 of this Notice of Violation regarding a written response describing how you intend to remediate the release and demonstrate attainment of an Act 2 standard.

Comments: On 5/06/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection in response to a complaint (CTS-397312) at the Clara Jacques 1 well plugging site in Wharton Township, Fayette County. This inspection also follows-up to IR 4186065, where violations were issued against severe tire rutting observed in the access road.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) was entered into between the Department and Diversified on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the Well Site after in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216; after completion of plugging operations.The following was observed during the inspection:A Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the site entrance along Five Forks Road (photos 1 and 2). An additional RCE is installed where the access road meets the well site, in accordance with the E and S plan drawing. The RCE adjacent to the well plugging site is laden with sediment (photos 15 and 22). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed on site in the locations shown on E and S plan drawing (photos 9, 12, 17, 19, and 20). Significant tire rutting remains throughout the access road. Due to the soft and damp soil conditions that appear to exist on site, the Department recommended in IR 4186065 that the operator consider additional E and S control measures as necessary, to prevent accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring on site. Well plugging equipment was observed on site, however plugging operations do not appear to be occurring at the time of inspection. A puddle with swirly rainbow sheen was observed adjacent to well plugging rig. This swirly rainbow sheen remained intact when disturbed, which is a known indicator of a petroleum-based release.The Department identified an access road cross-culvert at the time of IR 4186065 (photo 23). No loose sediment was observed in the cross-culvert during this inspection. However, the Department recommended in IR 4186065 that the operator take necessary measures to ensure that the cross-culvert is protected from sedimentation.Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued in IR 4186065 shall remain outstanding. Additional violations shall be issued for failure to adequately protect the cross-culvert shown in Photo 14 and for failure maintain the RCE adjacent to the well plugging site. Additional volations may be forthcoming against the swirly rainbow sheen released adjacent to the well plugging rig.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/13/2024 to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Cecil Township, Washington county. 78a73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78a and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/13/2024
Violation Code: 78a73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78a and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected.
Violation ID: 8198421
Permit API: 125-29100
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Cecil Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/13/2024
Comments: The Department conducted an inspection of this well on 8/13/2024 after being notified by Range that the production casing failed during stimulation activities. At the time of the inspection equipment was being mobilized off site, and stimulation activities were completed. According to Range, anomalously low treatment pressures were observed while fraccing stage 64 of the 6H on 8/9/2024 at 7:17am. The Operator cut sand and started to flush when the low pressures were observed, and kill plugs were then placed in the production casing at 6531' and 6426'. A pressure of 2801 psi was observed on the backside of the production casing during the incident. Per Range, no anomalous pressures were observed on other casing annuli, nor were anomalous pressures observed on other offset wells. Range informed the Department during the inspection that the issue appears to be above the kill plug locations, and a log was scheduled to be run later in the week to determine the location of the failure. - The Department was not notified of the incident until 8/12/2024 at 3:45pm. This is a violation of 78a.73(c) which requires immediate notification to the Department in the event that anomalous pressures are observed during stimulation activities. - According to Range, a failure of the production casing was the cause of the observed anomalous treatment pressures. The failure of the production casing during stimulation is a violation of 78a.73(a). - The Department requests that Range submit as part of their Notice of Violation response a copy of the logs that are scheduled to be run that will be used to determine the location of the production casing failure. The Department also requests copies of stimulation records for stages 54 through stage 64 for the 6H.

Comments: On January 31, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection at Inflection Energy TLC Well Pad due to a reported spill. Inflection Energy Zac Subra left a message for DEP representative Brad Kline at 1150 explaining that a rented GPU dump had a washout due to a gush of sand causing a leak of production fluid to form. The leak overflowed the containment and impacted an area of snow and pad surface near the southwest corner of the pad. The area of impact was about 25 yards by 10 yards. Conductivity of free standing liquid in the secondary containment for the GPU was over range of the Oakton multimeter. The maximum conductivity range for the meter is 20,000 uS/cm. The well pad surface was screened with a soil conductivity meter and the conductivity ranged from 800 uS/cm to 2,800 uS/cm. The production fluid did not appear to flow off the well pad edge. Inflection Energy then began to vacuum out the secondary containment and, remove to contaminated ice snow near the GPU. Mr. Subra said the Penn E&R will be out to the well site to delineate the area of impact on February 1, 2022. The DEP recommends beginning the Act 2 process due to the unknown volume of the spill.

Comments: On September 18 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 3491397, 3387914, 3514511, 3543627, and 3595504. The findings were as follows:According to the Order issued to the operator by the Department for this site, the Operator shall completely restore the well site within 9 months after plugging.The well site was not restored during today's inspection. The site was not exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. According to the landowner, the site has not been restored to pre-existing contours.The well was plugged on October 7, 2021 according the the plugging certificate submitted by the Operator for this well. As such, the Operator was to completely restore the well site no later than July 7, 2022. E and S Plan has not been received by the Department as previously requested in IRs 3262679, 3387914, 3514511, 3543627, and 3595504.No E and S Plan was found on site. Although there has been additional growth since the Department's last inspection in July of 2023, lack of adequate uniform vegetation is still observed due to multiple areas of exposed soil and rock. There are several bare spots throughout the former well site that are lacking adequate uniform vegetation. No E and S BMPs are installed on site.The ground appears to be seeded in most areas, but 70% uniform vegetation has not been achieved at this time. Vegetative growth may be hindered by the amount of rock and gravel on site. The Department recommends the Operator take necessary measures to ensure 70% uniform vegetative growth is achieved for restoration of the site.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding.

Comments: On May 27, 2026, the Department conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation (CSE) at the former location of the MAWC well site in Springfield Township, Fayette County. This inspection also follows up to IR 4183832, where the violation issued in IR 4095466 was left outstanding for failure to restore the well site by 10/30/2025, in accordance with the 5/01/2025 amendment of the 12/16/2021 CO and A.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) was executed between the Department and the operator on December 16, 2021. The First Modification to the COA was entered on May 1, 2025. Paragraph 3i of the 12/16/2021 COA states: "M4 shall immediately commence work to completely restore the Well sites upon execution of the First Amendment and complete restoration of the Well Sites by October 30, 2025, in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas act, 58 Pa.C.S. 3216, the site restoration regulations set forth in 25 Pa. Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. M4 shall submit form 8000 PM-OOGN0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," within sixty (60) days of restoring the Well Sites."Site restoration is to be conducted "as closely to original conditions as practicable, including restoration of original contours and capability of supporting land uses existing prior to drilling of the Well(s) by October 30, 2025, unless M4 obtains a signed and notarized written consent of the landowner to leave the Well Site in an altered state".The following was observed during the inspection:The former well site appears to overall exhibit approximately 50% vegetative growth during this inspection, although some isolated locations on site remain sparsely vegetated (photos 17 and 18). The temporary stabilization applied on site appears to be adequate at the time of inspection. Erosion control blanketing was installed north of the former well pad in a location that appeared to be prone to receiving high volumes of stormwater flow. The erosion control blanketing appears to have encouraged vegetative growth to take hold in this location (photos 13-15). However, further review is required by the Department to determine if the feature observed in this location is approved, pre-existing, and/or discharges stormwater in a manner that will not result in erosion. Additional apparent third-party vehicle tracks were observed at the former well pad location (photos 7, 20, and 21). The Department recommends that the operator continue to document any third-party disturbances occurring on site, take reasonable efforts to stop them while promoting continued vegetative growth, and prevent accelerated erosion from occurring on site. The portion of the super silt fence located within the site boundaries appears to be repaired and maintained in accordance with current regulations, at the time of inspection (photo 16). The Department recommends that the operator continue to maintain the super silt fence in accordance with manufacturer specifications, while it is in-use during site restoration.No loose sediment was observed in the channel that empties into the Sediment Trap that reportedly pre-exists well site construction (photo 19). Based on observations from this inspection, the violation issued in IR 4095466 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's Bellows L (03-078) Well site in Columbia Twp, Bradford County on 6/26/2019 at 1130 hours. The weather was 79 degrees and mostly sunny. The inspection was conducted in response to a notice of the release called into the regional office. Kris Perritt (Repsol), Matt Bryan (Repsol), Andy Senefelder (Golder), and others from Repsol and numerous Bishop Brother's employees were all onsite. It was discovered that when the truck drivers were offloading the production tanks they were also taking water from the frac tank to top of their tanks. The tank was too low so when they would collect from the frac tank they were using the man-hole cover on the side of the tank to place hose through there to collect. This was reported to not have been properly closed. When the tank filled back up, production water was released from the cover. Upon this release, it was also discovered that the secondary containment around the frac tank had failed allowing most of the fluid within to be released to the pad surface. A reported 2 barrels was released. The release flowed into existing stormwater that had collected on the surface. In the area closest to the containment, I was obtaining readings of Over ranged on my PCSTestr35. Over Range represents a greater than 19.99ms/cm field reading. In the areas furthest from the release it was still clear that mixing had occurred and field readings of ~4.0-5.0ms/cm were still obtained. Repsol emptied the tank, removed it from the containment and marked the large area for excavation of 1-2 inches below the surface. Two vac trucks were deployed onsite to remove impacted waters. A dozer and skidsteer would be used to excavate pad material and dispose into roll-off tanks. A supervac(hydrovac) was also being deployed to excavate in the sensitive areas around the wellheads. A new containment was scheduled to be installed later today. Due to the findings throughout the course of the inspection, violations of the following are cited against API # 015-23288: 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 35 P.S. 6018.301 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a)

This was reported to not have been properly closed. When the tank filled back up, production water was released from the cover. Upon this release, it was also discovered that the secondary containment around the frac tank had failed allowing most of the fluid within to be released to the pad surface. A reported 2 barrels was released. The release flowed into existing stormwater that had collected on the surface. In the area closest to the containment, I was obtaining readings of Over ranged on my PCSTestr35. Over Range represents a greater than 19.99ms/cm field reading. In the areas furthest from the release it was still clear that mixing had occurred and field readings of ~4.0-5.0ms/cm were still obtained. Repsol emptied the tank, removed it from the containment and marked the large area for excavation of 1-2 inches below the surface. Two vac trucks were deployed onsite to remove impacted waters. A dozer and skidsteer would be used to excavate pad material and dispose into roll-off tanks. A supervac(hydrovac) was also being deployed to excavate in the sensitive areas around the wellheads. A new containment was scheduled to be installed later today. Due to the findings throughout the course of the inspection, violations of the following are cited against API # 015-23288: 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 35 P.S. 6018.301 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a)

Complaints Tracking System (CTS) ID# 391708 is tied to this release within CTS.Seneca Resources notified the DEP via the reporting hotline that on 8/25/2025 at 1400 hours a plunger system cracked on the well pad releasing 15 to 20 gallons of produced water to the gravel pad surface. Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a release of at least 5 gallons of a mixture of produced fluid and stormwater was discovered on the well pad following a re-frac on the 5H well. The notification also stated that a contractor, Tobias, would excavate the impacted pad material. I met with company man Levi Lee upon arriving on location. He showed me the location of the release. It rained steadily during this inspection. Tobias had already scraped a thin layer of gravel off of the top of the impacted area at the time of inspection. Mr. Lee said that Creston Environmental was also present to take samples and characterize the release. Some areas of the impacted pad area were more damp than others. No standing fluid was observed in this area of the well pad. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the pad material according to the Hanna soil conductivity meter ranged from 0.41 mS/cm to 2.86 mS/cm. The higher EC readings were found closer to the well heads and the lower readings were taken farther away from the well heads toward the southeast pad edge. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Violations noted.Violations remain outstanding for the release from June 1, 2026. These violations will be closed upon demonstration of Act 2 remediation standards.

Comments: The weather was 60 degrees F and overcast at the time of this inspection. The above-referenced gas well is currently listed as Active in eFACTS. At the conclusion of testing at the above-referenced well, pressures were measured with a crystal pressure gauge and recorded prior to opening each annulus vent. The results of this monitoring indicated that 0% LEL and 0% Methane was measured during the inspection. No New violations were noted at this inspection. All violations are continued from original date sited.

Permit API: 129-26861
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Derry Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/18/2024
Comments: On September 18, 2024 the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Diversified's Davenport Well Site located in Derry Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3774486 where violations were issued for an 18-20 barrel release of production fluid from a production tank on June 4, 2024.At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared stabilized with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed and the production tank that was leaking during IR 3774486 has since been removed from the well site. A well tag was fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it, and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges was observed coming from or near the wellhead. The area where the production tank once (where the spill originated), the slope that the spill traveled down, and the area downstream where the spill pooled up at now appears to be backfilled, seeded and mulched pending vegetative growth. In addition, at the edge of the downslope area right before a forested area began, some black fencing was observed.Several soil conductivity readings were taken in the spill areas (0.0418 mS, 0.0362 mS, 0.0054 mS, 0.0137 mS, and 0.0602 mS) and are significantly lower than the soil conductivity readings taken in the same areas at the time of the spill (Soil conductivity readings taken on 6/4/24 documented in IR 3774486: 1.35 mS, 1.454 mS, Over Range, 7.63 mS, 5.51 mS, and 4.90 mS). Upon inspection of the fence, two areas appeared to be compromised. A stake appeared to be snapped and the fence appeared to be pushed down by sediment, at this time, there did not appear to be any evidence of the sediment overtopping the fence and no erosion or sedimentation was observed behind this section of fence. Another section of the fence right behind a small tree appeared to not be trenched and a gap was observed between the bottom of the fence and the ground. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed behind this section of the fence a this time either.The Department is recommending the Operator promptly properly implement and maintain the temporary erosion and sedimentation (E and S) best management practices (BMPs) to prevent any pollution from occurring.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to properly implement and maintain E and S BMPs. In addition, violations issued during IR 3774486 shall remain outstanding until the Act 2 Report is submitted, received, reviewed and approved by the Environmental Cleanup and Brownfields (ECB) Program.

Comments: On 3/15/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Folta well site. It was 30 degrees and mostly cloudy when I arrived on location. Snowfall had impacted the region in the last 48 hours. Most of the snow was cleared from the pad surface. Ice, water and mud puddles were scattered across the pad surface. I field tested some of the water/mud puddles using a Hanna Groline meter with results under 1.0 mS conductance on the north side of location. A 60' x 40' x 3" deep mud/water puddle on the southeast corner of the pad field tested at >4.0 mS conductance. The upper limit of the meter is 4.0 mS. I field tested the water puddle with an Oakton PCTS 50, the result being 10.09 mS conductance. I collected sample number 9551-047 from this location for laboratory analysis. A road grader was spreading gravel on the pad surface and was progressing towards the water puddle with elevated conductance. I contacted Eric Hottenstein and reported the elevated conductance water. Eric stopped the road grader from filling in the puddle and was going to get personnel on site to address the elevated conductance puddle.Six existing wells have been shut in during the drilling and completion of four new wells. The new wells have had the surface and intermediate sections drilled. A big rig is expected on site within about three weeks to drill the four new wells to total depth. Well permit numbers are posted at the entrance to the access road. No bubbling was observed in the well cellars. Work crews were on site removing the GPUs and production equipment in order to make additional room for upcoming fracking operations. Due to snow cover, site stabilization could not be assessed during the inspection. PCSM features have not been installed at the site. The ESCGP was issued on 10/1/2010 and expired on 10/1/2015. It has not been terminated with the department yet.The DEP recommends the following:1. Because of the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface. 2. That Chesapeake submits for a new ESCGP for the site and followup with permitting to confirm any need for additional measures at the siteI left the site at 1120 hours.

Comments: On October 24, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at the STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. DEP spoke with Profrac Company Man Mike Reel and he said they were fracking the 1005H well at the time of inspection. The DEP observed multiple areas of staining adjacent to the containment for the fracking rig. The areas were screened for conductivity with a soil conductivity meter and two areas resulted in over range conductivity readings. The upper limit of the soil conductivity meter is 4.0 mS/cm. The first area is adjacent to the frack pumps off the east side of containment. This area of high conductivity is about 12' x 20'. The second area is adjacent to 1 frac tank and 2 gas buster tanks. This area of high conductivity is about 10'x10'. Soil sample 0651-139 was collected from the 10'x10' area. The volume of this spill is unknown because it is uncertain how much was spilled under the frack rig containment. The DEP pointed out the previously mentioned areas to Mr. Reel and he said he would have someone begin scraping up the areas immediately. DEP then placed a phone call to STL Resources Seth Rodriguez to inform him of the findings from the inspection. The DEP recommends assessing the area of elevated conductivity and updating DEP of the findings. Due to the unknown volume of the spill, the DEP recommends pursuing an Act 2 remediation. The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad on January 8, 2022. STL Resources is continuing to monitor and vacuum the water that is accumulating in the northwest and southwest stormwater vaults. This water is being pumped into frac tanks onsite. The water was not at a level where it could be screened for conductivity with the field meter in either of the stormwater vaults. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 22.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 25.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 26.2 uS/cm. Seep 1, 1a, and 3 were dry and could not be screened. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 31.7 uS/cm. Seep 4 was not screened due to the current condition of the seep screening area. This area is being driven through by ATVs checking on the freshwater waterline for the Sturgis South stimulation. The area is constantly being driven through to refuel the pumps on the waterline. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 24.7 uS/cm. The infiltration berms 2, 3, 5, 8, 10, and 11 along the access road are well vegetated and appear to be functioning correctly. Infiltration berms 1, 4, 6, 7, and 9 along the access road are vegetated but, the areas that are holding water have little vegetation and do not appear to be functioning correctly. Infiltration berm 1 off the northwest corner of the pad appears to be holding water and not functioning correctly. Infiltration berm 2 off the northwest corner of the pad and the infiltration berm off the southwest corner of the pad are lacking vegetation in the infiltration area. The DEP recommends working on the infiltration berms that are not functioning correctly and reseeding the infiltration berms that are lacking vegetation to prevent an erosion event. The areas of staining along with the elevated levels of conductivity outside of containment on the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b). Additional violations could be assessed pending results from the soil sample collected. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227 and 3306834

Permit API: 003-22581
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 1/21/2026
Comments: On January 21 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Midas Well Pad (NOT previously approved on 10/28/2021) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 1/20/2026 (CTS 394728). Present during the inspection was operator representative Jim Noon.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel.At the time of inspection, there are 4 total active wells on the well pad. Each well appeared equipped for production with a well tag present. No fluid leaks or spills were identified at the surface around any of the well heads or cellars. The production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks. The GPUs appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks.During the inspection, Mr. Noon guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Noon the release occurred on 1/20/2026. He stated the release occurred from a hose failure on a portable heater onsite. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 10 gallons of glycol onto the graveled well pad.Mr. Miller stated remediation had been completed and all impacted gravel/material had been removed and placed into drums. The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the spill was in an approximate 15 foot by 30 foot area adjacent to the portbale heater near the GPUs. Conductivity readings were taken in the area of the release/remediation with readings of 0.04mS, 0.03mS, 0.06ms, and 0.04mS being obtained. These readings appeared comparable to the background reading of 0.03mS.Based on observations from this inspection and information provided by the operator, it appears that the spill has been remediated in accordance with current regulations. The Department requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Violations are being issued as immediately corrected.

Comments: This well was stimulated on 5/17/2022 and is currently being produced with a pump jack. The operator information is displayed on the pump jack. Earth disturbance associated with reclaiming this pit and installing gathering lines alongside the spur road to the location has not been temporarily stabilized. A film of oil is evident on numerous trees along the southern edge of the location (beyond the pit). Stained soil with elevated specific conductivity (SPC) is also evident along various pathways across the forest floor downslope of where the pit was located. Unconventional: Yes
County: Clearfield

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-10-11
Comments: Doug Kepler of Seneca Resources called and reported a mixed brine/water spill of 1 barrel to the Department on October 10, 2019 at 1600. Mr. Kepler stated that crews were onsite cleaning up the spill as he was reporting it to the Department. Chapter 78a.66(b)2 states that all spills and/or releases should be reported to the Department within 2 hours after detecting or discovery of the release. I conducted an incident site inspection on October 11, 2019 with Kyle Kline of Seneca Resources at D-17 COP-B well pad. According to Mr. Kline, a well tender was onsite the previous day plunging well (033-26887) when a float got stuck on the separator. Pressure built up over time causing fluids to be released through the rupture disc located on the GPU separator. During my inspection I viewed the separator, the impacted area adjacent to the seperator, and the roll off box containing the impacted materials. I conducted field screenings using a soil probe randomly throughout the excavated area. Screenings ranged from 0 uS/cm- 220 uS/cm. Approximately 2-3 cubic yards of impacted materials were viewed inside the lined roll-off box. Please note, that Seneca Resources sent the Department an email on October 15, 2015 revising the initial spill volume from 1 barrel to 0.5-0.75 barrels of produced fluids released. This information was revised based off the well tenders report of claiming that the plunger system brings 1-1.5 barrels of produced fluids with each cycle. According to the well tender about 50% of the fluids went to the tank and the other 50% was released to the pads surface. Based off the Departments inspection, the Department concurs with this spill volume correction. Violations have been noted and have been immediately corrected.

Violation ID: 8283038
Permit API: 031-23676
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Monroe Township
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 7/29/2026
Comments: Today, Johnson Well Service (JWS) arrived on location accompanied by a Weldbank Energy cement truck. JWS rigged up the cementing equipment and circulated/washed down the well in an attempt to gain additional depth; however, no additional depth was achieved. JWS subsequently requested an attainable bottom at 2,781.51 feet. The Department granted attainable bottom based on the following: -The Gamma Ray log provided to the Department indicated no strata bearing oil or gas below 2,727 feet. -An attainable bottom of 2,781.51 feet allows for placement of cement at least 50 feet below the deepest known oil- or gas-bearing formation. Weldbank Energy then placed a 135-sack Type I cement plug (27-barrel slurry) from 2,781 feet to 2,070 feet. The contractor then mobilized a second load of cement and placed an additional 140-sack Type I cement plug (28-barrel slurry) from 2,070 feet to 1,332 feet. JWS will return to tag and verify the top of cement on the following day.
